name: Save what you learned
description: Seeded default. Asks the agent to keep lessons and repeatable commands after a turn.

action.text: Most turns need no note: reply "nothing to save" unless this turn produced knowledge that a future agent or a teammate could not get from the code or git history, such as the root cause of a non-obvious bug and its fix, a decision with the reason behind it, a constraint or gotcha, or where something non-obvious lives. Never save routine work: installing or configuring tools or MCP servers, running commands, editing files, progress or status, or anything this turn merely did. Before saving, search with note_search and update the existing note (note_update, by id) instead of adding a near duplicate. Write a specific title and a body that stands alone for a reader with no context: what, why, and the repo-relative paths involved; no transcripts or step lists. Save as many notes as clear this bar and none otherwise: one focused note per finding, repository-specific knowledge in the repository scope and knowledge useful across projects in the global scope. Write each note in English and add 3 to 5 lowercase tags, including synonyms someone might search for. Save a command sequence as a script (script_save) only when you have run it more than once and it will recur. Always pass project_path (the absolute path of the repository you are working in, its git root) to note_save, note_update and script_save: without it a note can land in the wrong repository. Reply briefly.
